This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make public comments on items within the subject matter jurisdiction of the council/agency board that are not listed on this agenda or are listed on this agenda as an item other than a public hearing item. Members of the audience will have the opportunity to address the
city council/agency board about public hearing items at the time the public hearing is held. Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the council/agency board is prohibited from taking action on oral requests, but may refer the matter to staff or to a subsequent meeting. The council/agency board will respond after public comment has been received. Each person or representative of a group shall be allowed to speak without interruption for up to five (5) continuous minutes, subject to compliance with applicable meeting rules. CITY OF AZUSA

  REGULAR MEETING
  MONDAY, NOVEMBER 21, 2016 – 6:30 P.M.

The City Council of the City of Azusa met in regular session at the above date and time in the Azusa Auditorium located
at 213 E. Foothill Boulevard, Azusa, CA 91702.

Mayor Rocha called the meeting to order at 7:30 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: CARRILLO

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo.
Staff Members: City Manager Butzlaff, City Attorney Hull, Management Analyst Lacasella, Neighborhood Services
Coordinator Quiroz, Chief Deputy City Clerk Garcia. Human Resource Director Ayala, Chief of Police Hunt.

REGULAR SESSION

Mayor Rocha called the meeting to order at 7:30 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, ROCHA
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: CARRILLO

ALSO PRESENT
Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo, Tresurer Vasquez.
Staff Members: City Manager Butzlaff, City Attorney Martinez, Management Analyst Lacasella, Neighborhood Services
Coordinator Quiroz, Chief Deputy City Clerk Garcia. Human Resource Director Ayala, Economic & Community
Development Director Christiansen, Public Works Director/City Engineer Bobadilla, Chief of Police Hunt, Director of
Utilities Morrow, Police Captain Fleming.

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Captain Sam Fleming
The invocation was given by Pastor Rick McDonald, Azusa House of Prayer.

PUBLIC COMMENT

Jorge V. Rosales stated that he was concerned that the agenda did not include the ceremonial swearing in of f Chief of
Police Steve Hunt, as well as not showing the correct start time of the regular meeting. He contends that it does not meet
the regulations of the Brown Act. He also commented on Item D-3 with regard to City Manager deferred compensation
benefits.

Carolyn Crawford thanked everyone for the Field of Glory Event. She stated it was all made possible through the Canyon
City Foundation and with the support of the City and sponsors Jan’s Towing, Grand Village, Azusa Greens, Comfort
Climate, Waste Management, Athens, Community Care Hospice, Harry and Connie Heflin, R.G. Business Associates, Dr.
Mark and Barbara Dickerson, Julie Beman, UCS Environmental, and Azusa Civilian Police

Julie Vasquezof Hope Community Church announced that they will be serving meals for the community and sent out a
general invitation to the community.. This will take place Thursday November 24, 2016, from 12:00 to 3:00p.m

City Manager Butzlaff responded that the ceremonial portion of the meeting was recorded on video tape for rebroadcast
for the community to view. He assured that they are in compliance with the Brown Act. He introduced Elizabeth Hull,
City Attorney who addressed the comment on the Brown Act.

Elizabeth Hull, City Attorney stated that, according to the Brown Act under the definition of meeting, the Act is clear that
ceremonials do not need to be stated in the Agenda.

City Manager Butzlaff, responded to Mr. Rosales, regarding Item D-3, he stated that the negotiation with the Deferred
Compensation benefits has nothing to do with the timing of his birthday which falls in January. However, it had more to
do with the scheduling and having time to meet with all of the council and discuss the benefits.
 REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

Councilmember Macias thanked Field of Glory committee for allowing him to participate in the event. He commented on
Chief of Police Hunt’s swearing in ceremony “well deserved and congratulations”. He wished everyone a Happy
Thanksgiving.

Councilmember Alvarez wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving; he also thanked the Veterans Committee and the
community for a successful event. He congratulated the new Chief of Police Hunt on his position. He commented on the
Christmas tree in front of City Hall, he requesting new LED lights for the tree to make it more visible.

Councilmember Gonzales wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving. He congratulated new Chief of Police Hunt on his
position and is looking forward to working with him in the future. He thanked the Field of Glory Committee and the
Veterans Ceremony for a successful event. He thanked the Chamber of Commerce for helping with the successful
Brentwood concert they had a full house at the Azusa Armory. He reminded everyone with the holidays to shop locally.

Mayor Rocha announced that they will be adjourning in memory of two longtime residents Christina Rodriguez and Mike
Lee. He wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving, and congratulated Chief of Police Hunt on his new position.

City Manager Butzlaff announced City Hall will be closed Thursday and Friday for the Thanksgiving Holiday. He
requested for Chief of Police Hunt may be excused and Captain Fleming take his place as Sargent at Arms for the night.

Mayor Rocha announced the winter shelter program for the homeless will run from December 1, 2016 through March 1,
2017. He announced the McDonald’s grand opening November 30, 2016 at 10:00a.m., December 3rd and 4th are yard sale
weekend. He announced December 4th Winter Family Fest from 9:00 a.m.to 4:00 p.m. at City Hall front lawn. He
announced December 5th at 5:30 the Tree Lighting Ceremony at City Hall front lawn.
